text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Parliament started a broad debate on European monetary union (EMU) based on parliament's grand committee's report.

- The grand committee's decision to study further the effects of and options to economic and monetary union (EMU) does not mean evading decision-making, but it is wise and responsible preparation, says committee chairman Erkki Tuomioja.
- Control over the state-owned companies should be concentrated to one ministry, a working group proposes.
- Chlorined drinking water increases the risk of cancer, a Finnish medical study shows.
- Homosexual couples' status should be improved, parliament's legislation committee says, but does not propose a right to register relationships.
- Justice ministry and interior ministry are planning to ban participation in criminal groups' activities to counter a wave of violence by motor cycle gangs in the Nordic countries.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Goverment will set a timetable for further studies on economic and monetary union (EMU) by mid-summer, Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto says.
- A merger between regional power companies Savon Voima and Kuopion Energia is likely, sector representatives say.
- Paper production will rise strongly in Europe in the next couple of years, european paper industry organization CEPI says.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Finnish banking institutions which have received bank support suffered from 800 million markka credit losses last year.
- Control over judges' arbitration functions and fees should be tightened, a committee at Justice Ministry says.
- A majority of MPs are prepread to abolish dog tax.
- Post-contraceptive or so called remorse pills are gainig popularity and doctors want to free them from prescriptions.
DEMARI
- Finland would lose its credibility if it were to reconsider the option a floating markka, socialist MP's say.
-- Nora Hallberg, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 292
